title: A Falsified Bar-Instability Criterion Reveals an Independent Disk-State Parameter from EFC-Modified Disk Kinematics
description: This paper empirically tests an EFC-modified Toomre-like stability parameter ΠEFC, which augments the epicyclic frequency with an entropy-flow term, as a predictor of bar morphology in disk galaxies. The bar-onset criterion is falsified (AUC 0.22–0.31, anti-correlated with truth), but the minimum Π within the disk window strongly correlates with independent disk-state observables (negative with stellar surface density, positive with gas fraction) across SPARC and xGASS samples. Πmin is thus registered as a Stage-1 candidate disk-evolutionary-state proxy on the joint (Σ, fgas) manifold.

Pi_EFC.description: EFC-modified Toomre-like stability parameter; smaller values indicate greater susceptibility to non-axisymmetric instabilities.

kappa_eff_sq.description: Effective epicyclic frequency including an EFC entropy-flow term with universal coupling \zeta constrained by \kappa_{\mathrm{eff}}^{2} \ge 0.

g_EFC_shear.description: Shear-based entropy-flow proxy used in v0.2 and onward; yields the physically correct sign (reducing stability where shear is negative).

g_EFC_v2proxy.description: Original longitudinal proxy (v0.1) for the entropy gradient; produces the wrong sign for bar triggering in rising rotation-curve regions.

sigmaR_Jeans.description: Jeans-inspired prescription for the radial velocity dispersion used as the primary model; constant 30 km/s fallback only.

Pi_min.description: Disk-window minimum of the stability proxy, used as the scalar observable for classification/correlation tests.

key_results.main_finding: EFC-BIC fails as a bar predictor (AUC 0.22 local v0.1; 0.31 resonance-aware v0.2; anti-correlated rankings), but Πmin robustly correlates with disk state (SPARC N=112: ρ[Πmin, log Σdisk] = −0.71, ρ[Πmin, fgas] = +0.65; xGASS N=98: ρ[Πproxy, log Σ∗] = −0.49, ρ[Πproxy, fgas] = +0.67), supporting Π as a Stage-1 disk-evolution parameter.
parameters_tested: ζ (zeta) coupling; physical bound from κ_eff^2 ≥ 0 (ζ_max ≈ 1.52 in sample)
entropy-gradient proxy form: d(v^2)/dR (v0.1) vs v R dΩ/dR shear (v0.2)
σR prescription: Jeans-based vs constant fallback
global resonance-aware windowing (ILR, CR, swing-X) in v0.2
α derived per-galaxy from EFC latency fraction (bounded [0.05, 0.95])
datasets_used: SPARC rotation-curve sample with SIMBAD bar labels (N = 43, SA/SB clean)
SPARC structural sample for Σ and fgas correlations (N = 112)
xGASS SDSS+Arecibo sample for external replication (N = 98)
SIMBAD morphological classifications (de Vaucouleurs bar code)

sealed_predictions.statement: At z ≈ 0 in late-type rotation-supported disks, the scalar Πmin (or Πproxy) is negatively correlated with stellar/disk surface density: ρ(Π, log Σ) < 0.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Blind external samples (N ≳ 200) with resolved kinematics and surface-density maps yielding |ρ(Π, log Σ)| < 0.2 (p > 0.05) after matching the analysis window and controls.

sealed_predictions.statement: At z ≈ 0 in late-type rotation-supported disks, Πmin (or Πproxy) is positively correlated with gas-mass fraction: ρ(Π, fgas) > 0.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Blind external samples (N ≳ 200) with independent MHI and M∗ showing |ρ(Π, fgas)| < 0.2 (p > 0.05), and persistence of null results under partial Spearman tests controlling for log Σ.

kill_criteria: KC1: On a large, blind external dataset (N ≥ 200 late-type disks) analyzed with the registered pipeline, both correlations ρ(Π, log Σ) and ρ(Π, fgas) are |ρ| < 0.2 with p > 0.05, and remain null under partial Spearman tests; this kills Π as a disk-state observable in EFC.

KC2: Demonstration that Π (or Πproxy) is a deterministic or near-deterministic function of log Σ or fgas alone (e.g., partial Spearman residuals -> |ρ| < 0.1 and no added explanatory power in multivariate fits), or that Π is strongly degenerate with gobs/RAR (R^2 > 0.9); this invalidates the claimed independent signal.

KC3: Replacing the Jeans σR prescription with direct resolved σR(R) measurements (stellar velocity-dispersion maps) eliminates the correlations (|ρ| < 0.2, p > 0.05); this indicates a pipeline artifact and kills the proposed observable.

KC4: Attempts to recover bar-prediction performance with ζ requiring κ_eff^2 < 0 in any part of the analysis window (i.e., ζ > ζ_max from physical constraint) are disallowed; persistent AUC ≤ 0.5 (or anti-correlated rankings) across independent labeled samples seals the failure of EFC-BIC.

KC5: High-quality IFU kinematics showing that the sign of v R dΩ/dR in disk windows is predominantly positive (contrary to expectations) across a representative sample would contradict the physical sign mechanism underlying gEFC in this formulation.
